title: Craft, practitioner and indigenous knowledge
summary: OpenAlex indexes academic publishing. Knowledge held by practitioners and transmitted by apprenticeship, demonstration or oral tradition is not merely under-represented here — it is absent, because it was never a paper. Nothing in this map can register a gap in it, including the gap that it is missing.

title: Humanities citations are only partly linked
summary: Reference linkage in OpenAlex runs near 95% for STEM but around 70% for arts and humanities, where monographs and non-English venues carry much of the scholarship. Every co-occurrence and citation measure in this project is correspondingly weaker there, and a computed gap in the humanities means less than the same number in molecular biology.

title: Literature before about 1970 thins out sharply
summary: Measured on 2026-07-27: OpenAlex holds roughly 1.38M works published in 1980, 1.05M in 1970, but only 305K in 1950 — about a fifth of the 1980 density. Historical analyses become progressively less trustworthy the further back they reach, and an apparent gap in older literature may simply be an unindexed one.

title: Historical slices use today's ontology, not the period's
summary: OpenAlex assigns topics with a model trained on the modern corpus and applies it retroactively. Filtering to works published before 1986 therefore does not reconstruct the literature as it was organised in 1986 — it projects the 2026 classification backwards onto it. Any claim about what was knowable at a past date inherits this distortion.

title: The computed gap layer failed its own validation
summary: The Swanson-style metric this project was built around does not reproduce the canonical result it was tested against. On pre-1986 data the fish-oil / Raynaud's pair ranks at top 30.8% of scored pairs against a pre-registered bar of top 5%. Two metric designs failed the same way: 'structurally close but rarely co-occurring' is dominated by adjacent clinical specialties that split papers between them rather than by holes in knowledge. No computed gaps are published as discoveries.

title: Some topics are dumping grounds for unclassifiable work
summary: OpenAlex assigns a topic to every work, so works with thin metadata land wherever the classifier defaults. 'Military Technology and Strategies' holds 22.3M works — 7% of the entire corpus — and 'Diverse Scientific and Economic Studies' holds 5.1M. These are artifacts of classification, not fields of that size, and any measure averaged over them is meaningless.
